newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold futures end mixed, bullion firmer.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold futures end mixed, bullion firmer.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based gold futures ended narrowly mixed in lacklustre trade on Tuesday, while spot gold prices rose modestly during Asian hours on short covering by overseas funds, traders said.

The stronger bullion price was offset by a continued firming of the yen against the dollar, however, and TOCOM's most-active August 1997 gold settled two yen lower at 1,345 yen per gram, its first weaker close for a week, while the other months ended four yen lower to one yen firmer.
Bullion closed at $380.80/$381.10, up from $380.35/85 quoted at the New York close.

One bullion dealer said stiff resistance was expected above $381 an ounce, although any sharp correction in the high-flying U.S. stock market after the Dow Industrials' recent foray above 6,000 could spark further gains from short covering.

Traders said TOCOM platinum came under pressure from long liquidation by individual investors amid sentiment that in the short term the yen was likely to continue correcting against the dollar and that $385 an ounce would prove a stiff resistance for spot prices.
August 1997 platinum ended four yen lower at 1,365 a gram, while the other months went out two to six yen weaker.
One trader expects gold and platinum to build a base near current levels, while a large overhang of speculative short positions is setting the stage for future short-covering rallies.
"I think we'll establish a floor soon," he said.

TOCOM palladium also slid, with benchmark August 1997 ending five yen lower at 425 yen per gram. Traders said weak demand from Japan's electronics sector and spot sales from Russia were likely to continue weighing on prices.
August 1997 silver was up 0.4 yen at 177.9 per 10 grams.
